title: Regular sequences in the image of a local homomorphism
statement: Let $\varphi:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism of nonzero commutative local rings, meaning that $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. Suppose $B$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], has finite Krull dimension $d\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and is Cohen--Macaulay, meaning $\operatorname{depth}(B)=d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Assume $\sqrt{\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B}=\mathfrak m_B$, where $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B$ is the ideal generated by the images of elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\sqrt I=\{b\in B: b^n\in I\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$. Then there exist $a_1,\ldots,a_d\in\mathfrak m_A$ such that $\varphi(a_1),\ldots,\varphi(a_d)$ is a regular sequence in $B$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The empty sequence is allowed when $d=0$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

source.place: Tag 06LC (lemma-find-sequence-image-regular). The selected source elements lie in the maximal ideal, since a regular sequence generates a proper ideal and a unit maps to a unit.

proof.text: Prove by induction on $d$ the stronger assertion with $\operatorname{depth}(B)\ge d=\dim B$ instead of equality, for every source local ring $A$ and every map satisfying the stated locality and radical conditions. This is an induction on dimension with both rings and the map variable. For $d=0$ use the empty sequence: its final quotient is $B\ne0$, so it is regular by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Equality of depth and dimension in the item implies the induction hypothesis on depth.

source.place: Tag 06LC (lemma-find-sequence-image-regular), dimension induction and its dimension-zero base case; Tag 00LF (definition-regular-sequence).

proof.text: Assume $d>0$. Regard $B$ as a finite module over itself, generated by $1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite], its associated primes form a finite set. This set is nonempty: $0$ kills $1\ne0$, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes] places $0$ in one associated prime. List them as $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_r$, $r\ge1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-associated-prime-minimal], every $\mathfrak q_i$ is minimal, using the Noetherian, local, finite-dimension and depth-at-least-dimension hypotheses. None equals $\mathfrak m_B$: every prime of a local ring is contained in its maximal ideal, so if that maximal ideal were minimal there would be no strict prime chain, contradicting $d>0$. Thus each $\mathfrak q_i\subsetneq\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 06LC (lemma-find-sequence-image-regular), reduction to avoidance of minimal primes; Tags 00LC (lemma-finite-ass), 00LD (lemma-ass-zero-divisors), 0BUS (lemma-CM-ass-minimal-support).

proof.text: Set $J=\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B$ and $\mathfrak p_i=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)$. Each $\mathfrak p_i$ is prime: the inverse image is proper since $1$ maps to $1$, and primality follows by applying $\varphi$ to a product. If $\mathfrak m_A\subseteq\mathfrak p_i$, every generator of $J$ belongs to $\mathfrak q_i$, hence $J\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$. For $b\in\sqrt J$, some $b^n\in J\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$, so primality gives $b\in\mathfrak q_i$. This would imply $\mathfrak m_B=\sqrt J\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$, contrary to the strict inclusion just proved. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] to $\mathfrak m_A$ and the finite nonempty family $\mathfrak p_i$ in $A$. It gives $a_1\in\mathfrak m_A$ avoiding every $\mathfrak p_i$. Therefore $x=\varphi(a_1)$ avoids every associated prime of $B$, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes] makes multiplication by $x$ injective. Locality gives $x\in\mathfrak m_B$. No finiteness hypothesis on $A$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 06LC (lemma-find-sequence-image-regular), prime avoidance in the source; Tags 00DS (lemma-silly) and 00LD (lemma-ass-zero-divisors).

proof.text: Let $\pi:B\to C=B/xB$ and $\psi=\pi\circ\varphi:A\to C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-quotient-nonzerodivisor-cm], $C$ is Noetherian local, $\dim C=d-1$, and $\operatorname{depth}(C)\ge d-1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], $C\ne0$, $\mathfrak m_C=\mathfrak m_B/xB$, and $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_B$; consequently $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_A$. Write $J_C=\psi(\mathfrak m_A)C=\pi(J)$, the latter equality following by taking images of the finite sums defining the generated ideals. For $c=\pi(b)\in\mathfrak m_C$ choose $b\in\mathfrak m_B$. Since $\sqrt J=\mathfrak m_B$, some $b^n\in J$, hence $c^n\in J_C$. Thus $\mathfrak m_C\subseteq\sqrt{J_C}$. Conversely $J_C\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$ by locality, and primality of $\mathfrak m_C$ implies $\sqrt{J_C}\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$. The radical hypothesis is therefore preserved. The source remains $A$, so it still need not be Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 06LC (lemma-find-sequence-image-regular), implicit quotient induction; Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM), final assertion, with one regular element; quotient local structure from lemma-characterize-local-ring and lemma-characterize-local-ring-map.

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis at dimension $d-1$ to $\psi:A\to C$, whose hypotheses were all checked in the previous step. It supplies $a_2,\ldots,a_d\in\mathfrak m_A$ with $\psi(a_2),\ldots,\psi(a_d)$ regular in $C$. Prepend $a_1$. Indeed multiplication by $\varphi(a_1)=x$ is injective in $B$. For each later index $i$, the quotient $B/(x,\varphi(a_2),\ldots,\varphi(a_{i-1}))$ identifies with $C/(\psi(a_2),\ldots,\psi(a_{i-1}))$ by sending the class of $b$ to the class of $\pi(b)$: the preimage of the latter generated ideal is exactly $(x,\varphi(a_2),\ldots,\varphi(a_{i-1}))$, as is seen by lifting its coefficients to $B$. This bijection respects multiplication by the next element. Hence every later multiplication is injective, and the final quotient is nonzero because the tail sequence in $C$ is regular. For $d=1$ the tail is empty and this quotient is $C\ne0$. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], the full image sequence is regular, completing the induction.

The statement is byte-identical to its N8 creation record. It matches 06LC and adds a_i in m_A (automatic); A is not Noetherian; d=0 is allowed. Five steps, no new nodes. Step 1 sets up the induction properly over (A,B,phi) with depth>=d, with the empty-sequence base case. Step 2: Ass(B) is finite (00LC) and nonempty (00LD, since 0 kills 1); its primes are minimal (0BUS, hypotheses met), and none equals m_B because d>0. Step 3: preimages are prime; m_A in p_i would force m_B=sqrt J in q_i, a contradiction; prime avoidance 00DS (any ring, r>=1) gives a_1; 00LD makes phi(a_1) a nonzerodivisor; locality puts it in m_B. Step 4: 02JN node gives C Noetherian local, dim d-1, depth>=d-1; the quotient-local node gives C nonzero and pi local; locality and the radical condition both pass to C. Step 5: quotient identification via the third isomorphism theorem; final quotient nonzero, including d=1. proof_deps equals the union of uses; no tag is used without a node. Small cases checked: d=0 Artinian non-reduced B; d=1; non-Noetherian A; radical hypothesis needed (k -> k[[t]]). No duplicate in the DAG (rg -L 06LC and image/regular-sequence searches).
